etymologies.etymologyHTML: From prefer +‎ -able, probably after Middle French preferable.

definitions.definition: Better than some other option; preferred.

quote.citation: 1756, George Benson, “The Præface. To the First Edition.”, in The History of the First Planting of the Christian Religion: Taken from the Acts of the Apostles, and Their Epistles. Together with the Remarkable Facts of the Jewish and Roman History; Which Affected the Christians, Within This Period., the second edition, volume the first, London:  […] J. Waugh and W. Fenner, page v:
quote.text: This work has been the care and ſtudy of ſome years; as far as health, and other affairs, would permit. For, this appeared, to the author, of as much greater importance, than any other hiſtory whatever; as morality and religion are more excellent, than any temporal affairs; and the hiſtory of true religion, præferrable to that of impoſtures and deluſions.

quote.citation: 2007, Ted Honderich, On political means and social ends, →ISBN, page 94:
quote.text: It is not to the point that an inequality of material goods, at high levels, may not be preferable to an equality of material goods at a lower level, precisely for such reasons as self-respect.
